title: Refresh-window + affinity merge causes short-lived cross-org session binding
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Summary:
A customer escalation reported that, during a burst of token rotations followed by concurrent refresh requests, sessions briefly gained access to resources scoped to a different org. This occurred on both Dedicated and Private deployments behind the edge proxy. The window is short (seconds) but reproducible under load and has high customer impact.

Observed behavior:
- Client A (org-A) rotates API key; rotation triggers background reconcile.
- Concurrent refresh requests from client B (org-B) that hit a cached route/affinity slot sometimes inherit the newly rotated key binding during a narrow race.
- Result: client B receives a valid session bound to org-A resource IDs for ~2-8s until the next reconciliation pass.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed in debug traces):
1) The refresh handler performs two operations: (a) compute namespace/tenant binding from the presented credential, (b) reconcile in-memory affinity slot (used by our edge fast-path) with the authoritative apikey mapping.
2) Under high concurrency the affinity slot update (writes) can be interleaved with a separate request's read, because we use a per-node in-memory LRU with a small lock window.
3) The rotate flow temporarily sets a transitional opaque token while the authoritative mapping is updated in the DB. The affinity slot can pick up that transitional mapping and return it to a different requester before the rotate flow finalizes the org mapping.

Impact:
- Customer visible: access to org-scoped resources for wrong org for up to ~8s.
- Affected deployment modes: Dedicated (GPU pools with edge proxies) and Private (VPC installs with node-local caches). Hosted customers are largely protected by an additional gateway check but similar misbinding could theoretically surface during conversion windows.
- Severity: high (P0) — escalated by on-call and customer success.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Use stress runner to spawn 200 concurrent refresh requests across two orgs while triggering key rotation for org-A every 5s.
2) Watch edge logs: correlate request IDs and affinity slot hits.
3) Check that request X for org-B returned bearer token with org=A claims in downstream service.

Mitigation (short-term):
- Hotfix (deployed to Dedicated customer clusters yesterday): make the affinity slot update atomic by promoting the per-slot lock to an RW-lock and ensure readers block during transitional token propagation. This reduces but does not fully eliminate window for complicated multi-node races.
- Temporary customer mitigation: reduced rotation frequency and forced stale-cache TTL to 0 for affected customers.

Proposed long-term fixes:
1) Change rotate flow to produce a two-phase commit for mapping updates: publish transitional mapping to slot only after DB commit and consensus acknowledgement from local cache managers.
2) Add authoritative gateway validation on every refresh that validates org-binding against central mapping (cheap read with local negative cache).
3) Add unit + fuzz tests that simulate rotate+refresh concurrency with multi-threaded affinity slot access.
4) Improve observability: emit "affinity-rebind" trace events with old/new mapping and request IDs, and add alert rule when affinity rebound rate exceeds 0.1%/minute.

Acceptance criteria:
- No cross-org bindings observed in stress tests under 3x production refresh+rotate load for 30 minutes.
- New integration test in CI that reproduces prior failure pattern is green.
- Rollout to Dedicated/Private via staged canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback knob.

Links:
- Incident Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02AUTH/incident-62001 (internal)
- Repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-stability/tree/eng/affinity-race
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11872
- Postmortem draft (private): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/ENG-62001+postmortem

Notes: this ticket bundles the long-term design and rollout tasks; the immediate hotfix PR is tracked separately and targeted for runtime-1.21.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Rodriguez: Initial report from CS about a Dedicated customer seeing wrong-org access during heavy rotate windows. Repro assigned to Victor.

2026-03-02 - Victor Chen: Reproduced locally with stress harness; captured tail logs showing affinity slot returned transitional mapping. Attached traces and request IDs in repro harness. Marking P0 and blocking auto-rotate for impacted customers.

2026-03-04 - SRE (Anita Patel): Deployed temporary lock-change hotfix to two Dedicated clusters; observed immediate drop in misbinds from 12/min -> 0.6/min. However, race still reproducible under extreme interleaving on single-host caches.

2026-03-06 - Security review (Liam O'Neil): This pattern is an authz escalation risk; recommend two-phase commit and gateway validation. Security review required: true. Added to next architecture sync.
2026-03-08 - Victor Chen: Implemented two-phase commit prototype and integration tests. PR opened (platform#11872). Running CI and extended integration (30m stress).

2026-03-10 - QA (Priya Singh): Integration stress for 30m at 3x load: zero cross-org responses observed. Found minor perf regression (p95 +6ms) under high QPS. Added perf acceptance check to rollout plan.

2026-03-12 - Maya Rodriguez: Scheduled canary rollout for 2026-03-14. Notifying affected customers of planned fix and potential brief reconcilation pauses. Follow-ups: add observability dash and create a KB article for CS.
